system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** general warranty cap. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the draft; none exists. | **Reject and mark up to AUD 6m** — the proposed fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject both thresholds and the deductible structure** — they materially dilute recovery relative to the buyer mandate. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**; Seller also proposes extending limitations to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24 months** for general claims, with separate periods for other claim categories. An 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval; none exists. | **Restore 24 months and confine it to general warranty claims** — neither the shorter fallback nor a universal time bar is authorised. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject the general-regime treatment** — ownership, authority and capacity require materially stronger and longer protection. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no adequate express carve-out is identified. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert a comprehensive non-waivable carve-out** — the buyer cannot accept contractual protection for intentional wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Deems the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records generally disclosed. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Delete general/deemed disclosure and require warranty-specific fair disclosure** — document dumping should not qualify warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; if any seller warranty uses a knowledge qualifier, limit it to **named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry**, never affecting title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 as drafted** — it improperly shifts diligence risk to the buyer and converts constructive knowledge into a defence. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller gives reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | Before Completion, obtain **effective written consent and evidence that all associated conditions have been satisfied**. | **Make effective unconditional consent and condition satisfaction a hard CP** — Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m/30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release will follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases of all security at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require payout and contemporaneous releases in the funds flow** — an unsecured promise of later release leaves the buyer exposed to existing debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD **420,000** Completion bonuses are not separately itemised; Seller calls them its matter, and on-costs are unstated. | Express seller-funded line item covering the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with clear funds-flow treatment. | **Add a specific seller-funded completion adjustment/payment line** — silence risks the company or buyer bearing a transaction-triggered Seller cost. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 records AUD **180,000** open, but payment status is not independently verified and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. | Broader indemnity covering all loss arising from failure to obtain ownership/transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving the contractual payment cure; verify the amount and obtain payment/assignment evidence. | **Broaden the indemnity and require cure evidence** — merely paying an unverified amount may not secure effective IP ownership or cover resulting loss. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; current materials do not establish access, exact scope, notification duty, breach, harm or loss. | Preserve relevant logs and evidence, continue a properly scoped investigation, provide regular updates and outcomes, and retain appropriate warranty/covenant protection without assuming a breach or quantified loss. | **Require preservation, investigation and update covenants while reserving rights** — the facts remain unresolved and support neither dismissal nor a premature liability conclusion. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Treats three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD **330,000 aggregate**—as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, accrual, avoidability and termination rights; no automatic Debt classification or purchase-price deduction. | **Keep classification open pending diligence** — the disclosure does not establish whether the costs are ordinary, accrued, unavoidable or terminable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Proposes that general limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated, and treats Tax/IP positions as settled under that general regime. | Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, specific indemnities and covenants, with no hidden override by the general warranty limitations. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture by claim category** — a universal overlay could unintentionally cap or time-bar separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the internal DD-012 share register as evidence that Seller holds 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of legal and beneficial ownership, valid issuance, authority and absence/release of encumbrances, in addition to the register and robust title warranties. | **Require independent title and encumbrance verification** — a supplied internal register is a source document, not conclusive independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller asserts Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the proposed general regime. | Treat both regimes as **open**, negotiate them separately, and make no assumption of unlimited liability or agreed resolution. | **Reject the assertion of settlement and reserve all positions** — the buyer playbook confirms no Tax/IP resolution has been reached. |
=== END ADVICE ===
